selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What main subjects does the passage say a person can understand by listening to the comparison?
questions.answer: It says the comparison helps explain the world, the human soul, the importance of religion, why life becomes like a prison without true religion, and how calling on Allah and believing in His oneness save a person from darkness.

questions.question: What choice was placed before the two brothers at the fork in the road?
questions.answer: They had to choose between a path with rules, safety, and happiness and a path with fewer limits but danger and misery.

questions.question: How was the road on the right described?
questions.answer: It was described as having order and discipline, with some difficulty, but leading to safety and well-being.

questions.question: How was the road on the left described?
questions.answer: It was described as having freedom from restraint on the surface, but leading to harm and unhappiness.

questions.question: What does the brother with good character say before taking his road?
questions.answer: He says that he puts his trust in Allah.

questions.question: Why did the better brother choose the right-hand road?
questions.answer: He chose it because he had good character and accepted order and rules.

questions.question: Why did the other brother choose the left-hand road?
questions.answer: He chose it because he was morally careless and wanted a path without restrictions.

questions.question: Which brother is followed more closely in this part of the story, and why?
questions.answer: The brother on the left is followed so the reader can see that what looks easy at first can actually become difficult and heavy.

questions.question: What lesson about freedom and rules can be inferred from the two roads?
questions.answer: It suggests that freedom without guidance can harm a person, while living by right guidance brings safety and peace.

questions.question: How does this opening comparison connect religion to a person’s life?
questions.answer: It shows religion as a guide that brings order, protection, and happiness instead of confusion and misery.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the comparison at the beginning of the passage?
questions.answer: Its purpose is to help the reader understand big truths about human life, religion, and the condition of the soul.

questions.question: Who gives direction to the two brothers when the road divides?
questions.answer: A serious man at the split in the road gives them guidance.

questions.question: What warning is given about the left-hand road?
questions.answer: The warning is that its lack of limits hides danger and misery.

questions.question: What promise is given about the right-hand road?
questions.answer: The promise is that even though it requires obedience and effort, it brings safety and happiness.

questions.question: What does the response of the good brother show about his faith?
questions.answer: It shows that he trusts Allah and is willing to follow what is right.

questions.question: What does the response of the other brother show about his attitude?
questions.answer: It shows that he prefers ease and unrestricted living over discipline and wisdom.

questions.question: How does the passage contrast appearance and reality?
questions.answer: It shows that the road that seems harder is actually better, while the road that seems easier is actually worse.

questions.question: What kind of person is the second brother described as being?
questions.answer: He is described as immoral, lazy, and drawn to comfort without responsibility.

questions.question: Why is the right road not presented as completely easy?
questions.answer: Because the passage teaches that the right path includes responsibility and self-control.

questions.question: What overall message about religion can be drawn from the brothers’ choices?
questions.answer: True religion guides a person to the better path, even when that path requires obedience and patience.

questions.question: According to the passage, what happens to the world and human life if true religion is missing?
questions.answer: The world becomes like a prison, and human beings become deeply unhappy.

questions.question: Which two expressions are presented as keys to freeing the human spirit from darkness?
questions.answer: Calling on Allah and declaring that no god deserves worship except Allah.

questions.question: Why is a comparison used instead of giving only direct statements?
questions.answer: A comparison makes the lesson easier to picture and understand through a story.

questions.question: What did the two brothers ask the man at the fork in the road?
questions.answer: They asked which road was the better one.
